body:
_Migrated from issue #1291, filed 2026-08-01._

Follow-up from the cross-family review on #1289 (fix for #1167). Not a regression — a cost characteristic worth bounding before someone hits it.

## What happens

Both consumers of `cwa_duplicate_cache` re-validate it against the user's live view via `filter_visible_duplicate_groups()`:

- `/duplicates/status`, polled every few seconds by every open admin/edit tab
- the `duplicate_notification` payload, built on every classic page render (#1289)

Each call runs `get_common_filters(user_id=...)`, which loads the user row plus **all** archived-book rows (`cps/duplicates.py:1085-1091`) and **all** hidden-book rows (`:1098-1103`). The 900-id chunking in `_visible_duplicate_book_ids` bounds SQLite parameters for the cached duplicate ids; it does not bound those two exclusion lists.

So the per-call cost scales with how much a user has archived or hidden, and it is paid on a timer regardless of whether anything changed.

## Why it wasn't fixed in #1289

The obvious mitigation — skip revalidation when duplicate notifications are disabled — is wrong. `layout.html:635` reads `duplicate_notification.count` unconditionally and shows the sidebar badge whenever `dup_count > 0`; `enabled` gates only the popup. Returning a zero payload early would blank the badge for anyone who turned popups off. That trades a live user-facing bug for a perf win, which is the wrong direction while #1167 is about the badge lying in the first place.

Mitigating factors that make this non-urgent: both filters short-circuit on an empty group list (`duplicates.py:381-384`, `:492-493`), so instances with no duplicates pay nothing; and the status poller already paid this cost continuously before #1289, so the page-render path did not introduce a new order of magnitude.

## Suggested shape

A short-lived per-user memoization keyed on cache version (`scan_timestamp`) + user id, shared by both consumers — so a page render and the concurrent status poll resolve visibility once, not twice, and repeated polls within the TTL reuse it. Invalidate on cache write and on archive/hide changes.

Worth measuring first on a library with a large archived set to confirm it's real before adding a cache layer.
title: Duplicate visibility revalidation is recomputed per page render and per status poll
